title: Late-event reconciliation using tombstone event stream for rolling-quota corrections
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Our rolling-window quota counters (hourly/daily/monthly) occasionally diverge from the canonical usage ledger when usage events arrive late from downstream ingestion pipelines (s3 delivery retries, kafka replays, or sporadic worker restarts). The current ad-hoc backfill path applies raw events directly which can double-count or miss adjustments when events are redelivered, and lacks a consistent audit trail. This causes transient incorrect throttles for some tenants and inaccurate billing after monthly close.

Goal: Introduce an idempotent reconciliation subsystem that uses an append-only 'tombstone-aware' event stream to compute deltas for affected rolling windows and apply safe compensating ledger entries and quota corrections with full auditability and minimal customer-visible disruption.
impact: Reduces incorrect throttling and billing discrepancies for multi-tenant customers affected by late-arriving events; improves trust in rolling-window guarantees and reduces manual billing adjustments. Expected reduction in billing correction tickets by ~85% for customers on reserved capacity plans.
proposed_solution:
1) Create an immutable ingestion log (tombstone stream) that annotates each usage event with: event_id, tenant_id, sequence_number, event_ts, original_ingest_ts, and tombstone_flag (true if the event represents a deletion/correction).
2) Build a reconciliation worker that: a) consumes the tombstone stream; b) computes the net delta per tenant for every impacted sliding window span (supports minute/hour/day granularity); c) writes a single idempotent compensation transaction (recon_tx) to the billing ledger referencing the reconciliation_run_id and the list of event_ids reconciled; d) marks events as reconciled to avoid repeat work.
3) Ledger changes must be 'compensating transactions' (not destructive edits) so ledger is append-only and auditable.
4) Provide a dry-run mode and a per-tenant rate-limited catchup path to avoid spikes in quota adjustments.
5) Expose a reconciliation dashboard in Console showing reconciliations performed, net deltas per tenant, and links to the raw events/PRs.
6) Add a safety envelope: if reconciliation would increase tenant usage beyond a grace_threshold for a short retention window, queue a manual review step or apply a temporary soft-quota so customer traffic is not abruptly dropped.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reconciliation worker runs in dry-run against last 30 days of events and produces deterministic delta outputs that match a reference Python implementation.
- End-to-end test where a set of synthetic late events are inserted: the reconciliation worker applies compensation transactions exactly once and rolling-window counters converge to the expected values.
- Telemetry: reconciliation success/failure rate, per-tenant delta histogram, time-to-reconcile distribution, and API audit links are visible in dashboards.
- Rollout gated behind a feature flag and an opt-in list of 'canary' tenants; no customer-facing throttles regress during canary.
- Security review completed and ledger write path authorized by KMS-approved service principal.
implementation_tasks: spec: finalize tombstone stream schema and retention policy
infra: provision append-only S3-backed event log + kafka topic for live consumption
backend: implement reconciliation worker with idempotency via reconciliation_run_id and reconciled_event_set metadata
ledger: add compensating transaction type and reconciliation reference metadata
api: expose reconciliation dry-run and apply endpoints behind admin RBAC
console: reconciliation dashboard prototypes and links to raw events
qa: synthetic harness for late/event redelivery scenarios
docs: runbook for oncall and billing ops describing how to surface and revert reconciliation entries
testing_plan: Unit tests for delta computation; integration tests that spin up a short-lived kafka + ledger test cluster and validate idempotency; fuzz tests for out-of-order and duplicate event deliveries; soak test across 48 hours to ensure resource usage remains bounded during bursty recon runs.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: recon_jobs_started, recon_jobs_succeeded, recon_jobs_failed, reconciled_events_count, per_tenant_delta_gauge, reconciled_lag_seconds. Alerts: P1 if recon_job_failure_rate > 5% for 15m or if average reconciled_lag_seconds > 1h for > 1h. Add dashboard tile showing reconciliation throughput and top-10 tenants by delta magnitude.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge schema and worker code behind feature flag. 2) Run dry-run on last 30 days for internal test tenants. 3) Enable for 5 canary tenants (reserved capacity) for 48h. 4) Gradually expand by 10x every 24h while monitoring alerts. 5) Full enable after 7 days of stable metrics. 6) Post-mortem and cleanup of temporary telemetry queries.
rollback_plan: If we observe >2% unexpected billing deltas or customer throttling regressions: 1) flip feature flag to dry-run mode immediately, 2) issue compensating reversals for any recon_tx written in last 72h using reconciliation_run_id audit trail, 3) open an incident with billing ops and notify affected customers via templated message.
notes: We must coordinate with the ledger team to ensure compensating transactions are first-class and carry reconciliation_run_id + event_id list. Consider sharding reconciliation workers by tenant hash to bound memory while computing sliding-window deltas. Retention of the tombstone stream should be at least 90 days for auditing. Prepare a customer-facing FAQ explaining late-event reconciliations and proration implications for billing cycles.
